frames.engine_frame: origin = gimbal pivot (intersection of both gimbal axes) at neutral; +Z = engine axis toward the injector (forward); +X = outer gimbal axis (ring pins in the fixed yoke lugs); +Y = inner axis (engine collar pins in the ring); right-handed
frames.pose: R = Rx(alpha) * Ry(beta): alpha about the fixed X axis (outer), beta about the ring Y axis (inner); thrust direction = R * (0,0,1)
frames.cad: STEP in mm, +Z forward; GLB in metres, +Y up (glTF)

rv1_station_of_pivot_m.src: RV-1 convention: nozzle exit at z = -0.03 m; z_station = pivot_station + z_engine

architecture.v: two-axis Cardan gimbal of the whole thrust chamber; split engine collar clamped in a 0.5 mm groove of the case at the pivot plane carries the inner pins (+/-Y); gimbal ring carries the outer pins (+/-X) running in 608-2RS bearings in two fixed yoke lugs on the thrust frame

pivot_location.v: at the mid-burn CG of the gimballed engine (wet CG 6 mm aft, dry CG 6 mm forward of the pivot)

pivot_from_injector_face_m.src: injector face is forward of the pivot

gimbal.reason: pivot trade (calcs/gimbal_trade.py v1, same engine, gnc.json v1 vehicle): the forward (injector-end) pivot gives a tail-wags-dog zero of 14.2 rad/s at 20 % thrust against the gnc.json requirement >= 25.0 rad/s, needs ~8.96 deg of range and a linear hinge-moment sum of 13.21 N m (lateral acceleration alone 3.925 N m); the CG pivot gives 33.2 rad/s (26.2 at 12.5 %), 6.69 deg range need and 4.832 N m. Cost of the CG pivot: the head (pintle actuator, torch, ports) sweeps the airframe and the actuators need an annulus beside the engine -> engine-bay ID 140 mm instead of 120 (see envelope) and a long feed hose.
gimbal.trade_tag: DERIVED calcs/gimbal_trade.py v1 (CAD v2 engine solids; head hardware layout of CAD v2, compacted in v3)

range_deg.note: commanded limit applies to the VECTOR norm sqrt(alpha^2+beta^2) <= 7 deg (request to GNC)

mechanical_stop_deg.src: conical stop: polyurethane bumper ring in the thrust-frame bore contacts the case 89 mm aft of the pivot
